doc.title: George "Pops" Foster and Mugsy Spanier Interview, 1957-04-21

title: Meeting Bix and the cornet team, 1921-25
summary: Mugsy on playing with Bix Beiderbecke in Chicago; Pops places Bix on the boats; Bix's style.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Bix Beiderbecke: hearing, copying and remembering him

blocks.x: Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. I wasn't working with the New Orleans Rhythm Kings, I was working on Clark Street. And I'd be down to New Orleans Rhythm Kings, Mike Frenzel, if they'd get off early, we'd go out to where Joe was working and sit around and listen. And by the fact, we started out originally as a cornet team. Oh, would you talk about that a little? I didn't know that. Well, sure. I was working at the Vista dance hall on 43rd Street three nights a week. Vytavec used to come out with me. I used to get five dollars a night, so we'd buy a couple of pints of gin. Vytavec would come out. How did you first get to know Vytavec? Through Eddie Condon. I think Eddie Condon brought him up at the Columbia dance hall when I was working on him. I stuck up with friendships. So we used to go down to places where Jimmy Noon was working on the Paradise. About when was this, Maxim? Around 1922. Around that time. And Vytavec, and I would sit in as a cornet team. I used to work at the rendezvous. That was in 1925. I'd work at White City. Get through with White City and go work in the rendezvous for one to six and more. Vytavec was in Charlie Strait's band. So Vicks would stay after he got through and we'd both play. So we'd have all breaks together. Like Louis and the other. Yeah. That's the first time I still have to do it in 1922.

He was working in Chicago on Charlie Strait. This was the winter of 22. He had a Peewee with him, a drum boy. He had a band at the Arcade in St. Louis on the Alice Street. Well, he was around 22. He was in Chicago. The winter of 22. No, he was in Chicago then.

22 of the winter. He was at the Arcade in 22. Because I'd run away with my first wife and I know I was in St. Louis. That's what I'm doing. Maybe you were in Chicago. I was in Chicago then. 22 of the winter.

He was at the Arcade in 22. Because I'd run away with my first wife and I know I was in St. Louis. Maybe you were there for a week. Yeah, possibly. Because I know he was working with Charlie Strait. Was he good by 1922? Was he?

He was really fooling around more with the piano. Wait a minute. I think it was 21. 21 because the year before I left my first wife. Because I played with the Trum Boy on, what's he called them? C Melody. C Melody. Yeah. Trum Boy. Bix was on piano then.
Bix played piano. And then Pee Wee. And I never know who he was. He was. He was. He was. He was. He was. He was. He was. He was. He was. He was. He was.
He was. He was. He was. He was. He was. He was. He was. He was. He was. He was. He was. He was. He was.

He was. He was. He was. We used to have a good turn. Bidebeck. Were you pretty good friends? Oh yes. But you really didn't play the same way at all? No. Entirely different. Entirely different. He played his style. Now just to say you were kind of at that stage influenced by Oliver. Who was he influenced by? I couldn't tell you. I couldn't tell you. I couldn't tell you. Bidebeck just had his own individual style. Who you were in? Spider-Man. I couldn't tell you who Bidebeck was influenced by.
